name: Force-Directed Graph Layout
problem_statement: Given a graph, compute a position for every vertex in 2 or 3 dimensions under a declared force model, so that connected vertices are pulled together and all vertices repel each other, producing a drawing that visually reveals clusters and hubs.

normalization: Project directed input to undirected for layout purposes.
Remove self-loops; they contribute no attractive or repulsive force between distinct vertices.
Collapse parallel edges by summing nonnegative weights; use unit weight when weight_mode=unweighted.

problem_inputs.name: dimensions
problem_inputs.description: Dimensionality of the output coordinate space.

problem_inputs.name: force_model
problem_inputs.description: Exact force law defining attractive and repulsive potentials; layout quality is only well-defined relative to a declared model.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Scale an edge's attractive force by its declared weight, or treat all edges uniformly.

problem_inputs.name: iterations
problem_inputs.description: Fixed iteration budget; null means iterate until the force_model's own convergence criterion is met.

problem_inputs.name: random_seed
problem_inputs.description: Seed for the stochastic initial layout and any randomized iteration order, for reproducibility.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether the iteration's own movement/gradient tolerance was met, or a fixed iteration budget was used with the achieved energy disclosed.

required_outputs.name: vertex_positions
required_outputs.description: Coordinate vector of length dimensions for every vertex.

required_outputs.name: final_energy
required_outputs.description: Total energy of force_model (sum of pairwise repulsive and edge attractive potential) at vertex_positions.

required_outputs.name: converged
required_outputs.description: Whether the iteration met its stated movement/gradient tolerance.

optional_outputs.name: energy_trace
optional_outputs.description: Energy value after each iteration, for diagnosing convergence.

solution_semantics.objective: Minimize the declared force_model's total energy function over vertex_positions in the stated dimensions.
solution_semantics.exactness: This problem has no exact mode and no unique global optimum; solution_quality=converged requires meeting the iteration's own stated tolerance, and solution_quality=approximate permits a fixed iteration budget with final_energy disclosed.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Not applicable; vertex_positions assigns exactly one coordinate vector per vertex.

validation_rules: Every vertex has a position vector of exactly dimensions real-valued coordinates.
final_energy recomputes from vertex_positions and the normalized graph under the declared force_model within numeric tolerance.
Given the same random_seed, parameters, and graph, two runs of the same implementation reproduce final_energy within tolerance.
Coincident vertex positions are permitted and are not treated as invalid.
edge_cases: A single isolated vertex may be placed at an arbitrary position; it contributes no attractive force.
A graph with no edges reduces to pure mutual repulsion with no attractive term.
Disconnected components repel each other but have no attractive force pulling them together, so their relative placement is constrained only by repulsion.
iterations=0 returns the initial layout as-is, with converged=false unless the initial layout trivially satisfies the tolerance.

correctness: final-energy recomputation under the declared force_model
dimensional and completeness checks on vertex_positions
run-to-run reproducibility under a fixed random_seed
